chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a man in the unrestricted area (al-hill), then entered the Sanctuary (al-haram). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not killed, nor fed, nor given drink, nor sold to, nor sheltered, until he exits the Sanctuary, and then the Legal Punishment (hadd) is established upon him.'

I said, 'So what do you say about a man who kills inside the Sanctuary, or steals?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Legal Punishment (hadd) is established upon him inside the Sanctuary, quietly, because he did not consider the Sanctuary to have sanctity.'
And Allah the Exalted has said: 'So whoever acts aggressively against you, inflict injury on him according to the injury he has inflicted on you.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for the one who is inside the Sanctuary.' Then he said: 'So there is no aggression except upon the oppressors.'

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The fixed Legal Punishment prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca), a sacred area with special legal status
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The unrestricted area outside the Sanctuary of Mecca
key_terms.فَلا عُدْوانَ إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ: Quranic verse reference limiting aggression to the oppressors

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a murderer who takes refuge in the Haram of Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi delineates the procedural distinction in applying hadd punishments based on the locus of the crime relative to the Sanctuary's sanctity, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding the inviolability of the Haram. The Imam clarifies that while a murderer from outside is detained and executed upon exit to preserve the Haram's peace, one who kills inside is executed quietly to reflect their specific disregard for the place's holiness. This legal nuance is grounded in the Quranic principle of proportional retaliation, ensuring justice is served without unnecessary disruption of the sacred space.
